title: First-job practical demonstration and signoff
audience: Trainee or new worker on the solar panel cleaning track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Perform the named task within an approved scope and site safety rules
Explain and demonstrate safe decisions in realistic work situations
Provide observable evidence of work quality and appropriate escalation

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the solar panel cleaning track. Panels are usually mounted on roofs or elevated structures and are connected to DC and AC electrical circuits. Panels can produce voltage in daylight even when the rest of the system is off. Cleaning on this track does not include electrical work, isolation of the system, opening enclosures, or cable or connector repair. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Learning context and safe boundaries
instruction.body: A trainee must complete a supervised small-room clean using the employer’s kit and checklist. The learner must follow the actual site induction, product instructions, employer procedures and supervisor direction. Do not undertake work beyond training or authorisation.

instruction.heading: Step-by-step field procedure
instruction.body:
1. Review the job brief, hazards, site rules and required PPE before touching equipment.
2. Select compatible products and tools using labels, surface guidance and the employer’s procedures.
3. Demonstrate high-to-low and clean-to-dirty sequencing while segregating tools and preventing recontamination.
4. Inspect the result against the stated acceptance criteria and correct defects within authorisation.
5. Complete handover, safe equipment storage and incident/exception reporting; the assessor records direct observations.

instruction.heading: Worked decision and reasoning
instruction.body: The assessor introduces a damaged power lead. Trainee must isolate the equipment, avoid use and report the defect. The correct approach is to identify the applicable instruction, protect people and property, and document any departure from the original work order.

instruction.heading: Practice and feedback
instruction.body: Perform a full supervised task with assessor checklist, corrective feedback and a repeat attempt if necessary. The trainer observes each step, asks the learner to explain their decisions, and gives corrective feedback before reassessment.

instruction.heading: Quality and completion criteria
instruction.body: Evidence must show accurate scope interpretation, safe sequencing, correct tool/product selection, respectful communication, and reliable handover. Critical safety failures require stopping the practical and retraining.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. Isolation and testing in this lesson apply to portable equipment only, not to a PV system. Electrical testing, isolation and repair of PV systems need a licensed electrician; in Victoria, Energy Safe Victoria guidance supports installation, maintenance and repair by licensed electrical workers, but not testing or who may isolate. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Review the job brief, the hazards, the site rules and the required PPE before touching any equipment.
Put on the PPE that the job brief and site rules require.
Select products and tools for the surface, using the product label, the surface guidance and the employer's procedures.
Clean in a planned order, from high to low and from clean to dirty, and keep tools apart to prevent recontamination.
Inspect the finished area against the stated acceptance criteria and correct any defect within your authorisation.
If a damaged power lead or other defect is found, isolate the equipment, stop using it and report it before resuming.
Store equipment safely, then complete the handover and report any exception or incident to the assessor or supervisor.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. Isolation and testing in this lesson apply to portable equipment only, not to a PV system. Electrical testing, isolation and repair of PV systems need a licensed electrician; in Victoria, Energy Safe Victoria guidance supports installation, maintenance and repair by licensed electrical workers, but not testing or who may isolate. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

qualityStandard: The job brief, hazards, site rules and required PPE are reviewed before any equipment is touched.
Products and tools are selected using labels, surface guidance and the employer's procedures.
The result is inspected against the stated acceptance criteria, and defects are corrected within authorisation.
Equipment is stored safely and any exception is reported to the assessor.
summary: A trainee completes a supervised small-room clean using the employer's kit and checklist while the assessor observes each step.
The practical covers preparation, product choice, clean-to-dirty sequencing, inspection against the acceptance criteria and handover.
A damaged power lead is isolated, kept out of use and reported.

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be checked before the first-job demonstration touches equipment?
options: The job brief, site rules, required PPE and compatible products, checked before any equipment is touched
The employer's equipment, which can be used before the brief is read and the trainee's own tools too
Only the cleaning product's brand, because the label is not needed and the product is used at full strength
A damaged power lead, which can be used carefully if the trainee is cautious and the job has to start on time

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do with a damaged power lead during the first-job demonstration?
options: Tape the lead and continue, since the room is nearly finished
Isolate the equipment, stop using it and report the defect
Keep using it carefully until the assessor leaves
Repair the lead with household tape and test it on the carpet

knowledgeChecks.question: What evidence shows this task was completed competently?
options: The trainee's own statement that the room looks clean and the trainee's own view of the work done
Attendance at the induction session alone and a signed form from the session leader that day
A supervised observation against the assessor checklist, with the result checked against the acceptance criteria
The time the trainee took, since speed shows competence, and how quickly the room was finished
